source: GetYourGuide checkout programme, experiment log in /work/checkout.html. Same calls and numbers as the case study.

calls.title: Hold-your-spot countdown: "We'll hold your spot for 30:00"
calls.ctx: A real reservation hold while the traveller pays. Not manufactured scarcity: the spot is actually held.
calls.why: Urgency reframed as service: we reserve for the user, not against them. The top single win of the programme.

calls.title: Price-expiry countdown: "Book now, the price rises when the timer ends"
calls.ctx: The hold-your-spot timer (EXP-01) had already shipped. This one tests the opposite framing of the same mechanic.
calls.why: A win that spends trust is a loss with a delay. One timer serves the user, this one threatens them. Killed on principle and on data.

calls.title: Promo code as a quiet link instead of an open field
calls.ctx: The code field is still there, one tap away. It just stops being the first thing a traveller sees before paying.
calls.lead: You would have fit right in.
calls.why: An empty field is an invitation to leave and go coupon hunting. A link keeps the option without issuing the invitation. Shipped.

calls.title: Single-page checkout: collapse every step into one view
calls.ctx: Every step of checkout on one screen, no navigation between them.
calls.why: 72% of the programme's uplift lived on mobile. You do not trade your best segment for elegance. The principle survived the kill: unbroken context, shipped as two named steps (EXP-02).

calls.title: Email-first continue, account creation deferred
calls.ctx: Ask for an email to continue and leave the account for later, to cut the wall before payment for new travellers.
calls.why: Flat is not dead when the qualitative signal survives. v2 paired email first with SSO and moved account creation after purchase: +1.1%, shipped.

calls.title: Reorder payment methods to match each market
calls.ctx: The same checkout in four markets, with the payment methods ordered by local preference.
calls.lead: You would have fit right in.
calls.why: Not a global truth, a local one. It became a per market rollout with a shared default, instead of forcing one answer on four markets.
